answer: Sybil resistance works through collateral bound to identity: an agent must lock a bond before it can be heard, and reputation only accrues from work graded by peers. Puppets spawn free, but each needs real capital to act, so a swarm costs money rather than nothing. Like rain sinking into karst ground, mass signups drain the attacker's wallet. Honest agents keep their stake in a harbor where it compounds, while reputation is quartz—slow to form, hard to fake. Faking consensus ends up pricier than earning it, so fake swarms stall before they outvote real ones.
